archive.headline: The week the ten-year touched 5.365% and returned
archive.summary: Weekend edition. archive.headline: Ten-year hit 5.365%. Minutes point to another hike.
archive.summary: Wednesday's ten-year touched 5.365%, its highest since 2002, before a $39 billion auction cleared at 5.300% with firm demand and the yield closed near 5.28%. The Dow and S&P 500 fell 0.66% and 0.22% and the Russell 2000 1.31%, ending winning streaks. The Fed minutes showed all 19 participants backed the September hike and most expect another by year-end, with October priced as a hold at about 83%. Gold hit a two-month low, European stocks lost about 1%, and Brent rose 2.4% on reports that Washington was weighing renewed strikes on Iran.

archive.headline: Records on lower yields. Korea falls, India hikes.
archive.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed at records on Tuesday, up 0.58% and 0.45%, with utilities up 3% and the ten-year closing at 5.267%, down about 4bp, even though the three-year auction went at 4.932%, the highest since 2006. The August trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion on record imports, euro-area retail sales rose 0.8% against 1.0% expected, India's central bank raised its rate to 5.5% and the Kospi fell about 1.5%. Brent was $101.45 on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and tanker incidents near Hormuz.

archive.headline: Nasdaq record. Ten-year at a 24-year high.
archive.summary: Brazil's Ibovespa jumped 7.7% to a record after Flavio Bolsonaro led the presidential first round, the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 on Nvidia and the S&P 500 at 7,773.95. ISM services prices paid rose to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, and the ten-year touched 5.349%, its highest since 2002, before closing near 5.31%. Brent fell about 2% to $100.3 on a G7 stock release, and the euro touched a 17-month low near $1.116 on French and Spanish politics.

archive.headline: Payrolls 29,000. Yields rose anyway.
archive.summary: September payrolls rose 29,000 against about 90,000 expected with a net 60,000 downward revision, unemployment 4.2% and wages +0.1%; October's Fed hike went to about 22% priced and the Nasdaq touched a record, but the ten-year closed about 3bp higher after Logan said half a point more is needed. The G7 agreed a 100 million barrel stock release, euro-area inflation printed 3.8%, Tokyo core CPI 2.7% and the dollar index reached a 17-month high.
